Italy draws wealthy Chinese property buyers with lifestyle ­and flat tax
article:
Italy is becoming a magnet for wealthy property investors thanks to its high quality of life and flat tax regime, and interest is also on the rise among mainland Chinese and Hong Kong buyers, property agents said.

Rome introduced a flat tax regime nine years ago to attract high-net-worth individuals, with foreign residents allowed to make a flat annual tax payment of EUR300,000 ($434,700) on all their overseas income under the scheme’s latest rules.

This has become a draw for wealthy investors. The number of participants in the scheme has risen from about 3,000 in 2024 to roughly 5,000 currently, according to Knight Frank.

The property consultancy has also seen a surge in the number of prime residential properties sold in Italy, with deals in the first eight months of the year up by about 140% compared with the same period in 2025.

The buyers are currently mainly from countries including the UK, US, Switzerland, France, India and the Netherlands, noted Knight Frank. But “interest in Italy is growing” among Hong Kong and mainland Chinese buyers as well, said Anna Ward, the firm’s international residential research lead.

For Hong Kong and mainland buyers, the tax considerations are a major attraction, though “lifestyle, diversification and long-term wealth preservation tend to be more important considerations”, Ward added.

About one-third of the prospective Italian property deals Knight Frank had in the pipeline for the autumn period were linked to tax-related relocations, the consultancy said in a separate report.

Demand for Italian real estate was also coming from European second-home buyers, as well as international owners seeking to expand their existing Italian holdings across additional destinations, agents said.

“Italy’s flat tax regime … continues to attract globally mobile wealth, with over 60% of prime international enquiries through Knight Frank now driven primarily by tax considerations,” Knight Frank said.

“This reflects a broader evolution in demand, from the introduction of the flat tax, through post-Covid lifestyle shifts, to the removal of favourable tax regimes elsewhere such as in the UK.”

Many non-EU residents relocating to Italy under the flat-tax regime also require visa arrangements, with relocation often going hand in hand with property acquisition and broader investment activity, according to Knight Frank.

The visa is open to non-EU citizens investing in Italian businesses, innovative start-ups, government bonds or philanthropic initiatives. Entry thresholds start at EUR250,000.

Other real estate brokers also expect more buyers from mainland China, Hong Kong and the wider Asia Pacific region to snap up Italian property assets.

Buyer enquiries for Italian real estate more than tripled in the second quarter of the year, compared with the preceding three months, according to property tech firm Juwai IQI, which has seven million property listings across 111 countries.

In the first half of 2026, Italy received the 14th highest number of inquiries from prospective Chinese buyers — ranking between Spain and Vietnam — said Kashif Ansari, Juwai IQI co-founder and group CEO.

The top three were Thailand, Australia and the UK, he added.

“We expect the number of Chinese living and buying residences in Italy to climb in 2027,” Ansari said. “At the top end, the flat tax and residency options are attractive. The Italian market is rising and luxury Italian lifestyle destinations are attracting Asia’s wealthy.”

“Chinese workers find opportunities in Italy’s economy, and nearly one-third of new residency permits going to Chinese citizens are for the purpose of studying in Italy,” Ansari added. “The Chinese are the largest non-EU group at Italian  universities.”

An estimated 290,000 Chinese citizens live in Italy, the fourth largest non-EU community in the country, he said. “Their numbers are climbing rapidly, by up to 8% per year,” Ansari said.

For Lisbon-headquartered Maia Properties, wealthy buyers are looking at Europe as a whole and picking the best base that suits their lifestyle and tax needs.

Although Chinese demand for Italian property is still an “emerging trend”, Luiz Felipe Maia, CEO and founder of the real estate broker, said “there is significant room for it to grow”.

title: New $30.4 mil research programme to develop sustainable construction technologies
article:
A $30.4 million research programme — involving a consortium of Woh Hup, Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT) and A*Star — has been launched to develop sustainable construction technologies and strengthen Singapore’s built environment sector.

This was announced at the Construction Technology Innovation Laboratory’s (CTIL) annual seminar at the SIT Punggol campus on Oct 1.

The three-year programme is supported by the Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2025 (RIE2025) plan, a five-year national plan aimed at strengthening research and development in Singapore.

The programme brings together the three consortium partners and seven other industry partners.

Industry partners will contribute project sites, operational expertise and validation environments to test and refine the technologies under actual construction conditions and accelerate their adoption across the sector.

Chiew Sing Ping, head of CTIL at SIT, noted that the built environment sector is facing increasing pressure to reduce embodied carbon while improving productivity and resource efficiency.

Lim Keng Hui, assistant chief executive of the Science and Engineering Council at A*Star, added: “Addressing sustainability challenges in the built environment requires innovation across advanced materials, engineering and AI-enabled optimisation.”

The programme comprises seven research projects focused on areas such as scaling up ultra-low embodied carbon concrete for wider industry adoption, and developing AI-powered design tools to help engineers optimise structural designs for lower embodied carbon, cost and material use.

By 2029, the consortium aims to reduce embodied carbon in urban development applications of new technologies by up to 40% compared with conventional construction methods.

It also seeks to create new business opportunities and deliver operational cost savings for industry partners.

Beyond research, the programme will support talent and capability development through the training of undergraduate and postgraduate students, as well as applied research opportunities for research staff in collaboration with industry partners.

Industry professionals will also have opportunities to build their capabilities through specialised training, industry attachments and technical seminars.

Yong De-Rhong, executive director at Woh Hup, said: “Our partnership with SIT, A*Star and industry partners gives us the opportunity to co-develop solutions that are not only innovative, but also practical and scalable for the construction industry.”

title: HDB resale prices dip 0.2% q-o-q in 3Q2026, while transaction volumes surge: HDB flash estimates
article:
HDB resale prices fell for a third consecutive quarter in 3Q2026. Flash estimates published by HDB on Oct 1 show that the Resale Price Index (RPI) dipped 0.2% q-o-q, narrowing from the 0.3% fall recorded in the previous quarter.

This came despite an improvement in market sentiment and an increase in housing enquiries following recent policy changes, noted Christine Sun, chief research and strategist of Realion (OrangeTee & ETC) Group.

On July 28, the 15-month wait-out period was removed for private property owners (PPOs) and ex-private property owners (ex-PPOs) buying a non-subsidised resale flat.

“Following the policy adjustment, there was a noticeable increase in buying interest and sales enquiries from private homeowners for HDB resale flats looking to right-size,” said Sun.

Resale transactions totalled 7,528 in 3Q2026, marking a 17.7% q-o-q increase.

Lee Sze Teck, senior director of data analytics at Huttons Asia, remarked: “While the PPOs and ex-PPOs were able to buy larger flats from July 28, the effect on prices was relatively muted in 3Q2026, alleviating concerns over outbidding and potential price surge by this group of buyers.”

HDB RPI and transaction volume

Larger flat types drive resale volume

An uptick in sales for larger flat types attributed to the spike in resale transactions, said Eugene Lim, key executive office of ERA Singapore.

A total of 1,822 five-room flats and 535 executive flats were sold during the quarter, up by 23.7% q-o-q and 39% q-o-q, respectively.

Additionally, million-dollar flat transactions also trended upwards in 3Q2026, with 597 resale flats changing hands for at least $1 million during the quarter. These transactions accounted for 8.5% of total resale flat transactions in 3Q2026.

ERA’s Lim noted: “Demand for million-dollar flats could have been driven by cash-flush private homeowners, who now face fewer barriers to entering the HDB resale market.”

Five-room and larger flats formed the bulk, with 353 transactions, up 24.5% q-o-q from 283 in 2Q2026.

Million-dollar flat transaction volume since 2012

Prices of million-dollar flats similarly increased in 3Q20256, with average prices standing around $1.16 million, 1.1% higher than $1.147 million in 2Q2026.

Additionally, the proportion of million-dollar flat transactions in non-mature estates stood at 11.4% in 3Q2026 — the highest thus far, noted Huttons’ Lee.

The most expensive transaction came from the sale of a five-room flat at The Pinnacle @ Duxton for $1.72 million in September, beating the previous record of $1.7 million set just days earlier.

Resale market to “face headwinds”

Realion’s Sun expects the HDB resale market to face headwinds following the increase in the income ceiling for BTO flats. From August 2026, the income ceiling was raised to $16,000 for couples and families and $8,000 for singles.

“The higher income ceiling would allow some to buy larger or pricier BTO flats, thus diverting more buyers away from larger, higher-priced flats in the resale market,” she added.

That said, Huttons’ Lee noted government changes to the allocation and distance priority for Primary 1 registration under Phase 2C from 2027. Under phase 2C, 60 places will be set aside, up from 40 currently.

In addition, 12 primary schools in Bukit Timah, Newton and Marine Parade will allocate more places to children living more than 2km away. For these schools, half of the places will be reserved for children living within 2km and the other half for those living beyond 2km.

The changes could benefit HDB resale flats in areas such as Bedok, Bukit Batok, Bukit Merah, Bukit Timah, the Central Area, Clementi, Geylang, Kallang/Whampoa, Marine Parade, Queenstown and Toa Payoh that are located near the 12 schools, according to Huttons.

Still, Lee expects the HDB resale market to bottom in 4Q2026.

The 13,484 flats reaching their five-year minimum occupation period in 2026 could see keen interest, with some centrally located and five-room flats potentially fetching at least $1 million.

Huttons projects resale flat transactions to total between 22,000 and 26,000 in 2026, while resale price movement may be between -1% to 1%.

Meanwhile, ERA anticipates resale transaction volumes to hover around 26,000 and an annual price growth between 2% to 5%.

“This aligns with the Government’s aim for a stable and sustainable HDB resale market, characterised by resilient buyer demand and healthy price growth,” said ERA’s Lim.

title: Buyers snap up new Hong Kong flats ahead of likely interest rate rises
article:
Hong Kong developers sold all of the more than 290 new flats they launched over the weekend of Sept 26–27, as buyers looked to lock in mortgages ahead of an anticipated rise in interest rates later this year, according to property agents.

The decision by the city’s major banks to hold rates steady despite the US Federal Reserve’s recent rate increase appeared to have given buyers a push, with many expecting local rates to rise in the coming months, said Derek Chan Hoi-chiu, head of research at Ricacorp Properties.

“A notable number of home seekers are actively entering the market to secure properties ahead of anticipated local rate increases,” Chan said.

On Sept 26, Chow Tai Fook-owned Sky Ace Enterprises shifted all of the 140 apartments it made available on its State Residence project in North Point, agents said.

The properties are a mix of one-bedroom to three-bedroom flats with between 28 sq m (301 sq ft) and 56 sq m (603 sq ft) of floor space. They were offered at discounted prices starting from HK$5.96 million ($970,800).

China Land Resources, meanwhile, found buyers for all 153 apartments at The Sterling II made available on Sept 27, agents said. The flats — ranging from 28.5 sq m (307 sq ft) to 67.8 sq m (730 sq ft) — were also offered at discounted prices of HK$5.43 million to HK$15.01 million.

The southwest Kowloon project also offered 35 flats via tender starting Sept 27.

“Developers are likely to push out launches quicker to avoid interest hike uncertainty,” said Norry Lee, senior director of projects strategy and consultancy at JLL in Hong Kong.

The latest sales performance is likely to provide some relief to the property market, after Hong Kong’s lived-in home prices fell 0.46% in July, halting a 13-month upswing, according to the latest official data.

The index tracking second-hand home prices slipped to 321.5 in July from 323 in June, the first decline recorded in 16 months, Rating and Valuation Department data showed.

The decline came weeks before the recent interest rate increase.

On Sept 17, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority lifted the city’s base rate to 4.25% after the US Federal Reserve had raised its target range to between 3.75% and 4% following its latest Federal Open Market Committee meeting.

The city’s three note-issuing banks did not follow suit. HSBC and Bank of China (Hong Kong) kept their prime lending rate at 5%, while Standard Chartered maintained its prime rate at 5.25%, according to separate statements from the lenders.

The Fed is set to meet again in late October. If it raises its target rate again, that could finally trigger Hong Kong’s lenders to adjust their own rates, analysts said.

“Despite potential upside risks in US interest rates and the likelihood of Hong Kong following suit, prevailing market optimism continues to support transaction activity,” Chan of Ricacorp said.

The timing of the launches also had a positive impact on the sales, according to Lee of JLL.

“Timing matters: with Mid-Autumn Festival this week and the National Day ‘golden week’ next week, developers are keen to catch this window for mainland buyers,” he said.

title: Passive Dividend Boost: 3 SGX Stocks Rewarding Investors in October 2026
article:
Three SGX-listed companies are preparing to reward shareholders with
dividends
this October.
PC Partner Group Limited
(SGX: PCT) leads off with its payment on 9 October 2026, followed by
Civmec Limited
(SGX: P9D) on 23 October 2026, and
Union Gas Holdings
(SGX: 1F2) on 29 October 2026.
These upcoming payouts run the gamut from steady, unchanged amounts to one that has more than doubled.
But as
income investors
know, a declared dividend is only as dependable as the cash backing it up.
Let’s look closer at the numbers to see how each company stacks up.
How did PC Partner more than double its dividend?
PC Partner reported revenue of HK$6.5 billion for the six months ended 30 June 2026, marking a 1.5% year-on-year (YoY) increase.
More impressively, net profit attributable to owners surged 117.9% over the same period to reach HK$545.5 million.
This earnings surge was driven by expanding margins rather than sales volume.
Gross margin widened to 16.5% from 10.5% a year prior, bolstered by rising average selling prices for video graphics array (VGA) cards.
While OEM/ODM VGA card sales jumped 73.9% on more orders for high-end cards, own-brand VGA revenue fell 9.2% as shortages in GPUs and graphics memory trimmed volumes by 18.4%.
On the back of these results, the board declared an interim dividend of SGD 0.10 per share (roughly HK$0.61), up substantially from HK$0.25 a year ago, though no special dividend was declared.
Crucially, this higher payout is firmly supported by cash generation.
Free cash flow surged to HK$2.5 billion from HK$648.7 million a year earlier.
As of 30 June 2026, PC Partner held HK$2.9 billion in cash against HK$1.3 billion in borrowings, putting it in a healthy net cash position of around HK$1.6 billion.
Looking ahead, management expects a more challenging second half as rising graphics memory costs and limited VGA card availability take a toll.
Nevertheless, leadership remains confident in delivering full-year revenue growth for 2026.
Can Civmec sustain its dividend without free cash flow?
For its full year ended 30 June 2026 (FY2026), Civmec saw revenue rise 11.4% YoY to A$903.0 million, while net profit attributable to owners grew 22.5% to A$52.1 million.
Growth was particularly pronounced in the Infrastructure, Marine & Defence segment, where revenue more than doubled to A$210.2 million.
The segment now includes Luerssen Australia (renamed Civmec Defence Industries), acquired on 1 July 2025.
The board declared a final dividend of A$0.035 per share.
Combined with the A$0.025 interim payout, Civmec’s full-year dividend stands at A$0.060 – matching its FY2025 total.
However, free cash flow swung to negative A$28.5 million, down from positive A$56.1 million last year.
Management attributed this dip to increased working capital tied up in heightened business activity and unbilled work in progress.
As of 30 June 2026, the company held A$54.6 million in cash against A$60.0 million in borrowings (excluding lease liabilities), putting it in a minor net debt position.
While Civmec held its total payout steady, operating cash flow in FY2026 was negative, covering neither capital expenditure nor dividends.
On a forward-looking note, a record order book, active tendering, and growing early contractor involvement engagements give the business decent visibility heading into FY2027.
What funded Union Gas’s maiden special dividend?
Union Gas posted a strong 1H2026, with revenue leaping 66.4% YoY to S$106.0 million and net profit surging 175.8% to S$12.0 million.
The main engine behind this performance was the liquid fuel division, which saw revenue jump 444.4% to S$51.7 million on higher sales volume and new contributions from the Dunman Road and Queensway service stations.
By contrast, the gas fuel segment remained flat at S$53.8 million.
Marketing and distribution costs barely moved despite a 66.4% jump in overall sales.
This solid performance led the board to declare an interim ordinary dividend of S$0.0048 per share, matching last year’s level, along with a maiden special dividend of S$0.0032 per share.
This brought total dividends for the half to S$0.0080 per share, up 66.7% YoY.
The payout was well funded by cash, with free cash flow expanding to S$25 million compared to S$1.3 million a year ago.
As of 30 June 2026, Union Gas sat on S$29.3 million in cash against S$7.6 million in borrowings, giving it a comfortable net cash buffer of S$21.7 million.
Management expects to finish FY2026 on a strong note, supported by full-year contributions from Dunman Road and nearly 11 months from Queensway.
Looking further ahead, two additional service stations in Marsiling and Jurong West are slated to open in 2027, expanding its network to five locations.
The group also strengthened its core footprint by acquiring two LPG retailers on 31 July 2026 for S$8.2 million.
Get Smart: How do you tell whether a dividend can last?
At the end of the day,
free cash flow
is the true lifeblood of any dividend.
Civmec maintained its full-year payout of A$0.060 in FY2026, but its free cash flow turned negative as operating cash flow itself was in the red.
On the other hand, Union Gas generated S$25 million in free cash flow, giving it the headroom to reward shareholders with a maiden
special dividend
alongside its regular distribution.
The distinction matters.
When you see a dividend, look past the declared amount.
Ask whether the business generates enough cash to keep those payments coming.

title: World-first green flight levy in Singapore adds to rising costs of air travel
article:
(Oct 1): Singapore will add to already rising costs of air travel as it introduces a world-first green levy on flights departing the city-state.

Passenger fares booked starting Thursday for services departing after Jan 1 will be subject to the additional charge of between $1 and $41.60 per ticket, dependent on the class and destination of travel. The fees are intended to fund measures to boost adoption of sustainable aviation fuel, or SAF, and help reduce the industry’s climate impact.

While the extra charge — which won’t apply to transit passengers — is minimal, the levy is being introduced as the airline sector grapples with higher prices of jet fuel as a result of the impact of the Iran war. Ticket prices will “inevitably have to rise”, the International Air Transport Association industry group said in a June report.

The Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore previously delayed the planned April introduction of the charges because of rising fuel costs, and has deferred the measure for cargo flights until next October.

Perth-based investor Chris Amour, who has taken only four flights to Singapore this year — a third of his usual number of trips — said the levy will only add to the cost burden on air passengers. “It’s basically like double-dipping,” said Amour, director of the Amourici Group, a property investment firm. “They’re already increasing the ticket price to compensate for the extra cost of fuel.”

Singapore’s approach to directly charge air passengers to finance work to accelerate adoption of less-polluting aviation fuel is in contrast with usage mandates in Europe and US tax incentives. The sector needs additional policy support with global production of SAF this year likely to be 2.4 million tonnes, equivalent to just 0.8% of jet fuel demand, according to IATA.

See also: UK airspace suffers second system failure, delaying some flights

The new levy will provide funds to a centralised agency tasked with purchasing sufficient volumes to hit an immediate target for SAF to meet 1% of Singapore’s overall demand. The country aims to increase that share to 3% to 5% by 2030.

While SAF is regarded as the major tool to decarbonise international aviation — which accounted for almost 1.2% of all greenhouse gas emissions in 2025 — high costs are a constraint and likely to limit uptake without further policy support, BloombergNEF said in its annual New Energy Outlook report.

See also: Qantas, Virgin hiking fares for AFL grand final shows duopoly’s grip

Efforts by Singapore will provide a boost to SAF suppliers, and the plan offers transparency “to all producers about how we could compete with the logistics, pricing and the traceability of the feedstock”, said Matti Lievonen, chief executive officer of Bain Capital-backed EcoCeres Ltd, which supplies renewable fuels.

Neste Oyj, which operates the world’s largest SAF refinery in Singapore, argues governments also need to continue to stimulate demand. Mandates being introduced in Asian markets will support the supplier’s plans to increase production to 2.2 million tonnes by the end of 2027, said Mario Mifsud, vice-president for renewable fuels sales and trading for Asia Pacific and EMEA.

title: Asian bonds follow Treasuries lower, stocks fall
article:
(Oct 1): Asian bonds declined and Treasuries held losses as elevated oil prices kept inflation concerns alive. Most regional stocks fell.

Government bonds in Japan, Australia and New Zealand slipped, while the Treasury 10-year yield edged up one basis point to 5.30%, remaining near the highest level since 2007 reached on Wednesday. US 30-year yields also climbed by one basis point, having reached the highest since 2002 in the New York session.

Oil steadied after gaining on Wednesday due to uncertainty over whether a recovery in Middle East flows can be sustained. Brent crude for December delivery traded near US$98 a barrel following a 1.9% advance in the prior session.

MSCI’s gauge of Asia Pacific equities dropped 0.5%, with decliners outnumbering gainers two to one. Japan’s Nikkei 225 index rallied 2%, while South Korea’s Kospi Index edged lower.

Tech remained in focus as Micron Technology Inc gave an upbeat forecast, but warned that rising compensation costs would weigh on profit margins. Japanese chip equipment makers were higher, but South Korean memory names were weak. Futures contracts for the S&P 500 Index climbed 0.4%.

Bonds remained in focus after global government debt posted its worst quarter since 2024 as oil near US$100 a barrel revived concerns about persistent inflation. Some relief came after the August reading for the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) preferred inflation gauge was softer than economists forecast, prompting money markets to cut the odds of an October interest-rate hike to less than 40%.

See also: Asian stocks rise, bonds steady before PCE data

Wall Street’s late swings underscored uncertainty over the outlook for equities despite easing inflation concerns and reduced expectations for another Fed rate hike. Attention now turns to US payrolls data due Friday, while traders start paying increased attention to the midterm elections in November to assess whether stocks can regain ground.

“We believe a strong earnings season and getting past the midterm elections are what will break the market out of its trading range and see new highs by year-end,” said Chris Zaccarelli at Northlight Asset Management.

Elsewhere, gold steadied around US$4,160 an ounce, while a Bloomberg gauge of the dollar was little changed after wrapping up its best month since March. In Japan, the yen fell 0.5% to 158.20 per dollar.

See also: Treasuries stabilise after sell-off, stocks slip

The key event on Wednesday was the inflation data. The US personal consumption expenditures price index excluding food and energy rose a less-than-expected 0.2%. The prior month was also revised lower. Consumer spending, meanwhile, increased at the fastest pace in more than a year, offering signs of cooling price pressures alongside resilient demand.

Wednesday’s data delivered a “goldilocks combination”, said Chris Osmond, chief investment officer at Fifth Third Wealth Advisors.

“Second-quarter growth was stronger than expected, consumer spending was more robust, the labour market rebounded sharply in September and the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge came in well below expectations,” he said. “The net effect is broadly supportive of risk assets and materially reduces the probability of an October rate hike.”

That helped a rally in US stocks for much of Wednesday. Short-dated Treasury yields were little changed, while 30-year yields gained six basis points. The yield on the 10-year climbed as much as seven basis points to 5.30%.

Global government bonds finished their worst quarter since 2024 as US$100 oil revived the threat of sticky inflation for the world economy. A Bloomberg index of the debt posted its worst quarterly loss since the three-month stretch at the end of 2024, when Donald Trump won a second term as US president and investors braced for a more expansionary fiscal policy.

“Bond markets are facing a triple whammy — big government spending, strong growth and geopolitical supply shocks,” said Jimmy Louca, senior portfolio manager at Australian Retirement Trust. “We’ve moved into a reflationary regime and the market has been slow to price it.”

title: OCBC Securities to drop minimum commissions for online trades on SGX
article:
OCBC Securities will be removing minimum commissions for online trades on the Singapore Exchange (SGX) from Oct 5. Wilson He, managing director of OCBC Securities, says the move is targeted at younger customers who tend to trade in smaller amounts. The number of active young investors, aged 30 and below, who trade with OCBC Securities has grown by more than 20% y-o-y as at Sept 30, 2026, outpacing the growth across the bank’s wider investor base.

According to OCBC Securities, more than 95% of their young investors trade exclusively online. The total number of trades made by these investors has risen by close to 60% y-o-y.

“We have a lot of serious and sophisticated investors that are trading with us,” He says. “They are trading $50,000 to $100,000. That kind of investor, if you remove the minimum commission, it doesn’t really matter much.”

“But to the smaller, younger investor, who is basically trying to get started with the Singapore market and to learn the ropes, they want to accumulate stocks, right? Every $500. Every $1,000. So, by reducing the minimum commission, we are really helping them to achieve that.”

He adds that the move aligns with the broader push by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and SGX to bolster the local equity market. MAS had convened a review group to propose measures to strengthen the Singapore stock market in August 2024, and the group’s final report was published on Nov 19, 2025.

One proposed measure, taking effect on Oct 5, is a reduction in the standard board lot size. Lot sizes for securities greater than $10 and up to $100 will be reduced to 10 units from 100 units, while lot sizes for securities priced above $100 will be reduced to 1 unit from 100 units. SGX had previously reduced the standard board lot size to 100 units from 1,000 units in January 2015.

See also: A strong start, but not the finish

“Our primary mission is to really support growth on the home market,” He says. “The market is also moving as part of the evolution of Singapore’s equity market. SGX is lowering the board lot size, which makes it very accessible for investors to start with a smaller amount. We believe that we need to work together with the government, with MAS and SGX, to support this.”

“If we reduce the minimum board lot size, for example, on the banking shares, but we still charge high [minimum commissions], all the returns would basically be eroded by the commission fee. But if you charge proportionally, it is good for young investors who are starting with $500 and $1000, and it will become really meaningful.”

The initial reduction in board lot sizes on Oct 5 will only apply to 11 stocks priced above $10. They include: DBS Group (SGX:D05 ) , Great Eastern (SGX:G07 ) , Haw Par Corporation (SGX:H02 ) , Jardine Cycle & Carriage (SGX:C07 ) , Jardine Matheson (SGX:J36 ) , Keppel (SGX:BN4 ) , OCBC (SGX:O39 ) , Prudential (SGX:K6S ) , SGX (SGX:S68 ) , United Overseas Bank (SGX:U11 ) and Venture Corporation (SGX:V03 ) .

See also: From 30 to 50: An analysis of the FBM KLCI’s past 17 years

“When we take this initiative, we are not only looking at the 11 counters; we are looking at all the SGX online trades as well,” He says. “You can build a portfolio for other counters as well, like the small- and mid-caps. We welcome you to build your portfolio.”

“Besides young investors, the removal of minimum commission for online trades and smaller board lot sizes benefits other segments too. For clients holding odd lots – often accumulated through scrip dividend schemes, where dividends are paid in shares rather than cash – these holdings will be easier to sell. Roughly a quarter of our clients’ Singapore share holdings are currently held in odd lots.”

OCBC Securities data shows that its young investors prefer more affordable counters. Seven of the top 10 shares traded in the Singapore market by OCBC Securities’ young investors year to date were priced under $10 a share. They include companies such as Singapore Airlines C6L and chip tester AEM AWX. The remaining three shares that are priced above $10 are DBS, OCBC and UOB.

While dropping minimum commissions would result in less revenue per trade, He says he is confident the cut will help OCBC Securities build long-term relationships with its customers.

“Whether the glass is half full or half empty depends on which angle you see it. If you take one transaction, yes, we used to charge $25; now I charge about $2. Per transaction, the margin is really much lower. But of course, we have to see what we can do to help customers achieve their goals and aspirations.”

Customers trade because they want to deepen their knowledge of the markets and build up their wealth. Instead of focusing on the margin per transaction, He prefers to focus on the lifetime engagement OCBC Securities can enjoy with its clients.

“Eventually, they will accumulate more assets with a trusted brokerage house and be ready for more sophisticated products. For example, share margin financing. We are here to support them. If they are ready to lend out their shares and to build a portfolio, we can lend out the shares,” He says. “We are looking at the long term. It is not about one trade, two trades, or maybe three to six months. We are looking for the lifetime value.”

title: SGX named World’s Best FX Exchange by Euromoney for second consecutive year
article:
SGX Group has again been named the “World’s Best FX Exchange” at the Euromoney Foreign Exchange Awards 2026, reinforcing its position as a leading global marketplace for managing currency risk.

Over the award review period from June 1, 2025 to May 31, 2026, total FX futures volume rose 19.3% year-on-year to US$5.89 trillion, with a peak monthly record of US$766 billion in March 2026. This momentum was anchored by flagship USD/CNH futures and INR/USD futures, with fast-growing leadership in other currency pairs such as KRW/USD, TWD/USD and THB/USD, shares SGX a press release.

SGX says that a key strength of its FX franchise is its combination of listed and OTC markets. Its benchmark FX futures sit alongside OTC execution and workflow capabilities through BidFX, MaxxTrader and SGX CurrencyNode, giving participants greater flexibility across execution and clearing. Solutions such as Exchange for Related Positions (EFRP) further connects the two markets, enabling clients to transfer OTC positions into SGX-cleared futures for enhanced capital efficiency.

Janice Kan, managing director and head of derivatives at SGX says that FX is increasingly about “connecting liquidity, technology and risk management” across a more integrated market ecosystem. “As trading and liquidity flow across both listed and OTC venues, institutional clients are seeking greater flexibility in how they execute and manage risk,” she explains. “Our focus has been to bring these capabilities together to deliver more efficient, seamless and resilient trading and hedging solutions.”

SGX has also expanded the ways investors can manage currency risks, launching micro-TWD contracts and Brazilian Real futures. In their debut month, BRL futures achieved a daily average volume of US$214 million, while the micro-TWD contracts reached approximately 1,000 lots in daily average volume within two months of launch. This expanded product shelf is supported by regular market research and resources for market participants including Aggregated Exposure Reports (AERs) that provide insight into participant positioning, market structure and liquidity conditions across listed FX futures markets, points out SGX.

SGX head of FX derivatives KC Lam says: “Effective market structure is about creating deeper liquidity, better price discovery and more efficient risk transfer. We are giving clients more precision in how they hedge, strengthening liquidity across different maturities and making it easier to execute when markets move quickly.”

See also: Skylink to issue two-year non-convertible bonds of up to $5 mil at 8% coupon rate

As at around 9.10 am on Oct 1, shares in SGX are down seven cents or 0.3% to $22.54. Ytd, the counter is up by more than 30%.

title: DBS appoints Blackstone Singapore chairman Gautam Banerjee to board of directors
article:
DBS Group Holdings has appointed Gautam Banerjee to the boards of DBS Group Holdings and DBS Bank, with effect from Oct 1.

Banerjee is currently chairman and senior managing director of Blackstone Singapore. Prior to this, he spent more than 30 years with PricewaterhouseCoopers, including nine years as executive chairman of PwC Singapore before retiring from the firm in December 2012.

He currently serves on the boards of Singapore Telecommunications and GIC Private Limited. His previous appointments include directorships of Singapore Airlines, Piramal Enterprises and Defence Science and Technology Agency. He also chaired the Singapore Centre for Social Enterprise.

A fellow of the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales and a fellow of the Institute of Singapore Chartered Accountants, Banerjee graduated from the University of Warwick, majoring in accounting and financial analysis.

See also: Great Eastern Holdings appoints former ComfortDelGro director to its board

DBS Chairman Peter Seah says: “Gautam brings extensive experience advising businesses and serving on major boards. Over the course of his career, he has developed deep expertise in governance, risk oversight and long-term value creation.

“His perspectives will further strengthen the Board as DBS continues to navigate an increasingly complex operating environment and deliver sustainable growth."

Banerjee will be a non-executive and independent director of DBS. According to a previous Bloomberg report, DBS is working on a succession plan for Seah, who has been the Singapore bank’s chairman for more than 16 years.

title: iFAST and Xtrackers by DWS launch four ETFs on SGX
article:
Investment and wealth platform iFAST Corporation is launching its first suite of four ETFs on the Mainboard of SGX in partnership with Xtrackers by DWS.

The ETFs are the iFAST Xtrackers Artificial Intelligence & Big Data UCITS Index ETF, iFAST Xtrackers Nikkei 225 UCITS Index ETF, iFAST Xtrackers MSCI Korea UCITS Index ETF and iFAST Xtrackers MSCI Taiwan UCITS Index ETF.

Expected to commence trading on Oct 22, the initial offer period of the ETFs is from Oct 1-14, with each share priced at $1. Besides investing in cash, eligible investors may tap Supplementary Retirement Scheme (SRS) funds to buy the ETFs.

iFAST group CEO Lim Chung Chun says that the firm’s foray into ETF issuance is a “natural extension” of iFAST's role in global investing while being in line with its goal to help investors make money. “A key part of this is bringing relevant global investment opportunities closer to investors through SGX, with the convenience of Singapore dollar trading, local market hours and other features that are relevant to Singapore-based investors,” he says.

See also: India lets wealth-focused funds with US$463 bil invest abroad

DWS is the asset management arm of Deutsche Bank, which operates its ETF business under the Xtrackers brand, which offers more than 300 ETFs across asset classes and markets.

Lim adds that by marrying the investment and product capabilities of established global fund houses with iFAST’s understanding of investors, advisers and distribution, iFAST can develop solutions that address selected gaps in the market and add value to clients.

The ETFs are structured under the Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) framework, a widely used European regulatory framework that sets standards in areas including diversification, liquidity and investor protection. For Singapore-based investors, locally traded UCITS ETFs may also offer different tax and estate-planning advantages compared with holding certain overseas-listed securities directly, depending on the fund structure and individual circumstances, notes iFAST.

See also: UBS brings institutional-grade investment access to Asia private wealth clients

The inaugural suite of ETFs provides exposure to artificial intelligence (AI) alongside the Japanese, Korean and Taiwanese equity markets. The Artificial Intelligence & Big Data ETF invests in companies involved in the development and adoption of AI and related technologies. The Japan, Korea and Taiwan ETFs provide broader market exposure, with Korea and Taiwan playing important roles in the global semiconductor and technology supply chain.

“In developing our first ETF suite, we focused on areas aligned with iFAST’s research views on long-term structural themes and where we see meaningful investment opportunities,” says Kenny Tjan, director of iFAST Global ETFs. “The selected exposures reflect our conviction in AI and big data, alongside the distinct opportunities offered by Japan, Korea and Taiwan.”

Sophia Kim, head of Xtrackers sales APAC at DWS, says: “As DWS’s global platform for ETF solutions, Xtrackers combines a broad product range with more than two decades of index investing experience. Together with iFAST’s local market knowledge and established wealth management ecosystem, we see strong potential to build on this collaboration and continue exploring solutions that meet the evolving needs of investors in Singapore.”

Shares in iFAST closed at $8.42 on Sept 30, down 10 cents or 1.2%.
